## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--exclude` needs an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment default, because the project's flag policy requires one for every new flag under `cli/`. The filtering logic itself has tests at the `collect` level and at the full-archive level.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` now skips any file whose basename matches one of the globs and logs each skip. The change also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds tests for parsing, filtering and the archive output.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` in the environment has no effect, because the new flag uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. That breaks `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`, which `AGENTS.md:3` points to: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set options through the environment cannot apply exclusions, so excluded files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, splitting it into a list of patterns, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with a case where the variable is set.
